description:
Scenario: a caller wires up SCT verification for TLS server cert validation. They get back `count = 0`. They have no way to distinguish:
- All SCTs were signed by logs the caller does not trust (UnknownLog).
- All SCTs had timestamps outside the log window (SctTimestampOutsideLogWindow).
- All SCTs had signatures that failed cryptographic verification (InvalidSignature) — this is the SECURITY-SIGNIFICANT case.
- The log key was malformed (LogKeyMalformed) — corrupted trust state.
- The cert DER was too long (CertDerTooLong) — impossible in practice.

These have wildly different security implications. "InvalidSignature" suggests a CT log signing-key compromise or a forged SCT — a serious alarm. "UnknownLog" suggests the caller's log list is stale — a configuration issue. The library MERGES these into the same zero-count outcome.

Maintenance consequence: every user filing 'why does my cert show zero valid SCTs?' will produce a long support thread because pkix-ct returns no diagnostic. The doc comment (verify.rs:357-364) admits this is intentional ('count vs policy threshold'), but the design is wrong: a verifier that drops error information is hostile to debugging.

Fix options:
1. Return `Vec<(usize, Result<&CtLog>)>` indexed by SCT position, letting callers inspect each one. Most flexible.
2. Add a sibling `verify_embedded_scts_detailed` that returns the same. Keep `verify_embedded_scts` as a thin wrapper for the common case.
3. At minimum, add a `tracing::debug!` per failure. Cheap, prelaunch-acceptable.

Architectural-completeness note (per AGENTS.md 'project phase'): the workspace is prelaunch. The complete shape for SCT verification is 'caller sees per-SCT verdict.' Shipping a count-only API now will fossilize into a permanent maintenance footgun. Breaking changes are free pre-1.0; design closure means picking the right shape now.
title: verify_embedded_scts coalesces all SCT verification failures into 'count=0' with no diagnostic
